ground_truth: The `verifiedProfileIdForAddress` function does not check if an address has been marked as compromised. This allows an attacker with a stolen private key to continue executing unauthorized actions even after the user has flagged the address as compromised.

When an address is restored after being marked as compromised, the `isAddressCompromised` flag is not reset to `false`. This prevents the restored address from performing any actions on behalf of the profile, defeating the purpose of the restoration feature.

The UUPS upgradeability pattern is implemented incorrectly. Inherited contracts are missing storage gaps, non-upgradeable base contracts are used instead of their upgrade-safe alternatives, and initializers are not disabled in constructors. These flaws could lead to storage corruption during a contract upgrade.
